_readme: Verified 2026-11-06 by A1 (Research). The UI may state a real-world fact only if it appears here. Many pages could only be checked through search-result snippets because direct fetches to wikipedia/skyvector/thenews were blocked by the sandbox network; each entry records the URL that supplied the information and a confidence level. Low-confidence entries must be shown with a caveat or not at all. Keys referenced by other modules are preserved.

airport.name.note: Verified via search-result snippets (direct page fetch blocked by sandbox network).

airport.iata.note: Also listed on Wikipedia, Great Circle Mapper and other aggregators.

airport.type.note: Listed as a domestic airport; no scheduled commercial service since 2013 (see history.lastFlight2013).

airport.elevation.note: Published values conflict: Wikipedia 135 ft; SkyVector 145 ft (airport) with runway ends 145 ft (RWY 02) and 130 ft (RWY 20); Great Circle Mapper / metarcentral 130 ft; airfield.directory 121 ft. eAIP value not seen. Display as approximate (130-145 ft).

airport.elevationRange.value: ≈ 130-145 ft (≈ 40-44 m) above mean sea level; sources differ
airport.elevationRange.note: Use this wording where a range is acceptable. SkyVector: airport 145 ft; runway ends 145 / 130 ft.

airport.timezone.note: Pakistan Standard Time, UTC+5. Not re-fetched in this pass; general knowledge.

airport.climate.value: Hot desert / semi-arid climate (Köppen BWh per Wikipedia)
airport.climate.note: Wikipedia's climate article describes the climate as semi-arid with very low rainfall; BWh vs BSh classification varies by dataset.

runway.designators.note: All aggregators agree on a single runway 02/20.

runway.length.note: airport-data.com, SkyVector and other aggregators agree; Wikipedia reportedly cites the PAA eAIP (June 2025) - eAIP itself not opened.

runway.surface.note: Wikipedia and Aviation Weather (acukwik) list asphalt; airport-data.com lists concrete. Do not display as certain.

runway.threshold02.note: SkyVector runway-end coordinates as seen in search snippet.

runway.derivedLength.value: ≈ 2,136 m between the two published thresholds (published length 2,133 m)
runway.derivedLength.note: Great-circle distance, spherical Earth R=6,371.0088 km. 0.01' rounding = about 18 m, so agreement with 2,133 m is within coordinate precision. See docs/FACTS_AND_SOURCES.md.

runway.derivedBearing.value: ≈ 25.5° true (RWY 02 end towards RWY 20 end); reciprocal ≈ 205.5°
runway.derivedBearing.note: Initial great-circle bearing 25.55°. Runway numbers 02/20 are magnetic (~20°), so a ~5° difference is expected from magnetic variation.

history.closed1998.value: Closed to commercial traffic in 1998 (for about ten years)
history.closed1998.note: Wikipedia; ARY News 2022 report also says closed in 1998 for ten years.

history.reopened2008.value: Reopened to commercial flights in August 2008 with PIA (19 August 2008 per Wikipedia)
history.reopened2008.note: Dawn reported an earlier planned reopening of 3 August 2008 (https://www.dawn.com/news/312232), so the start date shifted; use 'August 2008' unless the exact date matters.

history.lastFlight2013.value: Last commercial flight (PIA) in 2013; no scheduled commercial service since
history.lastFlight2013.note: The News (4 Oct 2026) and Wikipedia agree on 2013. Exact month not found.

history.closedPeriod.value: About 13 years without commercial flights (2013 to 2026)
history.closedPeriod.note: Headline of The News piece: 'set for revival after 13 years'.

revival.proposal.value: Proposed revival: runway extension from ~7,000 ft to ~11,500 ft for Boeing 777-class aircraft, with improved passenger facilities (proposed, per press reports)
revival.proposal.note: The News, 4 Oct 2026, citing unnamed PAA sources; corroborated by techjuice.pk and thepakistanconnect.com. A proposal, not an approved/funded project; no formal PAA statement seen. Which runway end would be extended is NOT stated - the game chooses one (simulated).

revival.proposalDate.note: Date taken from the search summary of the article; page itself not opened.

revival.uses.value: Developed as an alternate airport for Karachi, Sukkur and Nawabshah in case of emergencies or adverse weather (diversions); stakeholders likely to be consulted on regional flights (proposed, per press reports)
revival.uses.note: Per sources in PAA quoted by The News.

revival.stakeholderMeeting.value: Sindh Chief Minister and a PAA delegation reviewed Sukkur, Karachi and Hyderabad airport projects (Sept 2026); CM assured full cooperation
revival.stakeholderMeeting.note: Radio Pakistan; page date shows 19/20 Sept 2026 - verify before quoting a day.

constraints.encroachment.value: Land encroachment around the airport is reported as a constraint
constraints.encroachment.note: Gulf News: federal aviation minister was told encroachments were the main reason Hyderabad airport was not functional; Sindh minister said they could be sorted out soon. Report is from a 2022 meeting (date inferred ~25 June 2022 from a Tribune report of the same meeting). Not confirmed in the retrieved snippets of The News 2026 article.

constraints.landOwnership.value: Disputes over land ownership between aviation and provincial authorities have been reported for Sindh airport land
constraints.landOwnership.note: Gulf News reports a CAA land-ownership claim only for ~80 acres near Karachi airport. A Hyderabad-specific ownership dispute was NOT confirmed in retrieved snippets; a '1,473 acres' figure surfaced in one search summary and could not be corroborated - not used.

governance.federalSindhAgreement.value: Federal and Sindh governments agreed to work to make three Sindh airports (Sehwan Sharif, Hyderabad, Thar) fully functional; a technical committee was to survey them
governance.federalSindhAgreement.note: Gulf News; meeting c. June 2022 (date inferred, not shown in snippet).

org.operator.note: Also named as the body reviving the airport in The News (Oct 2026).

org.regulator.note: From 2024 the PCAA keeps regulatory functions.

org.split2024.value: PAA Act 2023; from 9 August 2024 the former CAA was reorganised into the PCAA (regulator), the Pakistan Airports Authority (airport operator) and a Bureau of Aircraft Safety Investigation
org.split2024.note: Profit / ProPakistani reports; the 9 Aug 2024 effective date is from one aggregated summary.

city.population2023.value: Hyderabad city: 1,921,275 (2023 census); district 2,432,540; second-largest city in Sindh
city.population2023.note: Boundary-dependent: citypopulation.de lists the 'Hyderabad City' taluka at 778,132. PBS tables: https://www.pbs.gov.pk/sites/default/files/population/2023/tables/table_2_sindh_districts.pdf. Say 'about 1.9 million (2023 census, urban agglomeration)'.

city.distanceKarachi.value: ≈ 136 km by the M-9 Karachi-Hyderabad Motorway (older Super Highway ≈ 160 km)
city.distanceKarachi.note: Wikipedia and AARoads give 136 km for the M-9; the 160 km figure is the older Super Highway.

city.mehran.value: 'Mehran' is a local Sindhi name for the Indus River, and a poetic name for Sindh
city.mehran.note: Wikipedia 'Mehran' / Indus River pages. Burnes (1835) said the name was little used by natives, so the AI assistant's name 'Mehran' is a cultural allusion, not an official term.

climate.recordHighMayJun.note: Wikipedia climate table (read via a mirror snippet); station/period not confirmed.

climate.typicalSummerHigh.value: Mean daily maximum in the hottest months (May-June) is roughly 40-41 °C
climate.typicalSummerHigh.note: Third-party sources disagree (June ≈ 40 °C WorldClim; May 41.3 °C elsewhere). PMD normals not retrieved.

climate.monsoon.value: Monsoon rain mainly July-September; traditional onset around mid-July, recently sometimes a month earlier
climate.monsoon.note: Express Tribune. Monsoon is the main rainy season; remainder of year is very dry.

climate.monsoonRainfall.note: From Wikipedia snippet; period not stated.

climate.dust.value: Dust and thunderstorms can occur in the pre-monsoon period; e.g. a July 2025 storm hit Hyderabad with ~42 knot winds
climate.dust.note: Seasonality not established: Wikipedia says dust storms are rare in May-June; Dawn reports one preceding monsoon rain in 2025.

aviation.codeE.value: ICAO Aerodrome Reference Code letter E = aeroplane wingspan from 52 m up to but not including 65 m (Boeing 777 is code E)
aviation.codeE.note: Wingspan alone defines the letter since Annex 14 Amendment 14 (outer main gear wheel span handled separately). Boeing 777 = code E: general knowledge, not confirmed in the retrieved snippets.

aviation.runwayWidthE.value: Minimum runway width for code 4E is 45 m
aviation.runwayWidthE.note: Annex 14 Vol I Table 3-1 (4E = 45 m) is from training knowledge; NOT confirmed in retrieved snippets - verify against the current Annex 14. Current runway width 30 m (code 4C/D range is 30/45 m).

aviation.resa.value: Runway End Safety Area (RESA): at least 90 m, recommended 240 m for code 3/4 runways

aviation.strip.value: Runway strip extends at least 60 m beyond each runway end (instrument runways)
aviation.strip.note: From an FAA/ICAO presentation snippet; check Annex 14 §3.4.

aviation.papi.value: PAPI (Precision Approach Path Indicator): lights showing red/white to indicate position relative to the approach slope; typical slope 3°
aviation.papi.note: General aviation knowledge; not source-verified this pass.

aviation.ils.value: ILS (Instrument Landing System): localiser gives lateral guidance, glide slope gives vertical guidance (typically 3°); categories I-III differ by decision height and RVR
aviation.ils.note: General aviation knowledge (ICAO Annex 10); not source-verified this pass.

pm.pmbok8.edition.value: PMBOK Guide, Eighth Edition (PMI), published November 2025
pm.pmbok8.edition.note: PMI page plus Learning Tree / PM Study Circle summaries.

pm.pmbok8.principles.value: Six principles: holistic view; value focus; embedded quality; accountable leadership; sustainability integration; empowered teams
pm.pmbok8.principles.note: From PMI (Spanish page) snippet; 7th edition had 12 principles.

pm.pmbok8.domains.value: Seven performance domains: Governance, Scope, Schedule, Finance, Stakeholders, Resources, Risk
pm.pmbok8.domains.note: Per third-party summaries (Learning Tree, 4PMTI, PM Study Circle); 7th edition had eight different domains (Stakeholder, Team, Development Approach & Life Cycle, Planning, Project Work, Delivery, Measurement, Uncertainty). Check the book before quoting.

pm.pmbok8.processes.value: 40 processes organised in five focus areas
pm.pmbok8.processes.note: Focus-area names not retrieved - do not display them.

pm.iso21502.value: ISO 21502: Project, programme and portfolio management - Guidance on project management (2020)
pm.iso21502.note: From training knowledge; not source-verified this pass.

pm.prince2.value: PRINCE2 (7th edition, 2023): principles, people, practices, processes; stage-gated, 'management by exception'
pm.prince2.note: From training knowledge; not source-verified this pass.

pm.apmbok.note: From training knowledge; not source-verified this pass.

pm.ipmaICB.value: IPMA Individual Competence Baseline (ICB4): people, practice and perspective competence areas
pm.ipmaICB.note: From training knowledge; not source-verified this pass.
